tickets.title: Headless Sonic runs on HUD's own pi worker extension without pi-roles
tickets.what: Design `.scratch/pi-worker/spec.md` (read whole; slice 1; owner approved removals R1–R4). HUD core builds the pi argv in process (no `pi-role`, no `--role-bundle`, no `--hud-*` flags) and writes a private per-job contract `<job>/pi-worker.json` read once by the extension via `HUD_JOB_DIR`. Add the worker extension (`src/harness/pi/worker/*` compiled to dist, thin `.mjs` entry; installed under `$HUD_HOME/pi-worker/` by core install, never `pi install`ed; checkout fallback for tests) with modules `contract`, `role-runtime` (verify model/thinking, fail fast; tool activation; role prompt section from `packages/hud-mcp/instructions/<name>.md` so the prompt matches today), `tools` (today's `hud.mjs` worker branch: hud_report/hud_progress/hud_lease for Sonic), `mistral-budget` (port of the owner's mistral-request-budget; images archived under the job dir), `web-search` (DeepSeek search/fetch; key from `~/.hud/credentials.env` `DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_API_KEY`, plus a one-time explicit `hud import` from the old key file), and a native writer of `tps` session entries in the same format pi-tps writes today (toktrack may read them; verify format). Add the in-code role defaults table keyed by today's `pi_role` names so role files that omit `model` keep today's model (the owner's sonic deepseek preset omits it). Lazy-load the dispatch graph in `src/worker/tools.ts` (orchestrator import costs ~80 ms). Route only headless Sonic through the new path; other roles stay on pi-role until later slices. No runtime legacy switch; rollback = revert.

acceptance.text: Parity dump (role section, active tools, model, thinking) for headless Sonic matches the legacy path except the approved removals; test asserts it.
Unit tests: contract round trip, argv golden, role-runtime on a fake pi, Mistral budget and DeepSeek search with stubbed fetch, credentials import, tps entry format.
Live: ~10 real Sonic jobs incl. a web scout run on the new path with reports; cost probe (offline pi, temp HOME) reports pre-model startup before/after.
Land gate passes.

tickets.title: Resuming a closed tab job does not emit a false 'failed | tab closed' notice
tickets.what: Observed twice on 2026-11-25 (job j3bd8576dccfd4ee1, imp on pi in a herdr tab): main sent `hud_send` to a closed tab job; the send resumed it (`continuation: resumed`) and the worker kept working in its tab, but the hud-mod wake immediately delivered `imp pi-worker: failed | tab closed | <old report summary>` while `hud_peek` showed `state: working`. Likely cause (verify, do not assume): the watcher's tab-close reaping (tests/unit/thin-mcp-watcher-reap.test.mjs: 'fails only a nonfinal job whose tab closes') sees the previous turn's tab/pane close after the resume has already made the job nonfinal, or the resume opens a new tab and the old one's close is attributed to the resumed job. Spec §2.1: silence or a display label cannot fail a live worker; a completion notice is not a read; no false failure. Fix so a tab close that belongs to a previous turn (or a tab the current turn does not run in) never fails or notifies the resumed job; a real close of the tab the current turn runs in still fails it as today. Out of scope: other notice kinds, reaping rules landed in pi-worker/03. Size: ~60 source lines, 1-2 tests.

acceptance.text: Test: a closed tab job is resumed by a send; the old turn's tab closes afterwards; no failed state and no failure notice for the job, and its next report settles normally
Test: closing the tab the resumed turn runs in still fails the job as today
Live try: hud_send to a closed imp tab job; the wake shows no 'failed | tab closed' line while the job works
Land gate passes

tickets.title: Hotfix: CLI workers start again; the invocation witness survives the owner's shell rc
tickets.what: Regression from pi-worker/03 (landed a34ee9fb), 2026-11-25: every CLI worker (claude, agy, codex, grok in herdr tabs) fails at dispatch with `error: unknown option '--hud-invocation=<uuid>'` (job j04ea7f4d3cd6234f, frontend-imp on claude). Cause: `harness-cli.ts` puts the witness shim dir first in the tab's PATH via `herdr tab create --env PATH=...`, then `herdr agent start ... -- <token> <args>`; the interactive zsh reads the owner's `~/.zshrc`, which prepends `~/.local/bin` (lines 15, 119), so `claude` resolves to the real binary and the argv token reaches it. Tests used shells without an rc. Fix in two commits, first one landable alone: (1) Hotfix: never put the token in the agent's argv. Carry it in the tab env (e.g. `HUD_INVOCATION_TOKEN`) that the shim checks; the witness file's exclusive create already makes it one-use. If the shim is bypassed, the real CLI starts normally and HUD finds no witness: it refuses adoption and reports it, as the fail-closed rule says. (2) Make the shim reachable after the owner's rc without editing any owner file: e.g. start the tab shell with a HUD-owned `ZDOTDIR` whose `.zshenv`/`.zshrc` source the owner's real ones (`$HOME/.zshenv`, `$HOME/.zshrc`, keeping their behaviour) and then put the witness dir first in PATH; other shells: decide the simplest equivalent or leave them on the refusal path and say so. Tests must use a shell rc that prepends a directory containing a fake agent (the real failure shape). Out of scope: any other pi-worker/03 rule. Size: ~80 source lines, 2-3 tests.

acceptance.text: A CLI worker launched in a tab whose shell rc prepends the real agent's directory starts and runs; the agent's argv never contains a HUD token
With the shim reachable, the witness is published and the supervisor adopts exactly that PID; with the shim bypassed, the job runs, adoption is refused and the reason is reported
No owner file (~/.zshrc, ~/.zshenv, ~/.bashrc) is written
Live try (main): dispatch one frontend-imp job on claude and one general job on agy after landing; both start and settle
Land gate passes

tickets.title: Hotfix: a reused herdr tab ID never makes a new job look closed
tickets.what: Observed 2026-11-25 20:33: fresh imp job j6daafb3598870be7 (pi) launched into herdr tab `w5M:t10` and the owner got `failed | tab closed` at once; the job kept working because pi then wrote its own STATUS. herdr reuses tab IDs (current tabs t1M..t1Y then t10). The watcher's `closedTabs` set (`src/runtime/watch-runtime.ts` ~L145, `rememberClosedTab`, `openRuntime().tab`, and the handoff `start(state, tabs)`) keeps an old close of `w5M:t10`, and `tabClosed = closedTabs.has(tab)` (~L679) then matches the new job's SESSION; with no pi pid yet the branch at ~L770 writes `failed / tab closed`. CLI jobs take the ~L705 path with the same stale fact and may be judged terminal; the reap path (~L483) also consults `closedTabs`. Fix the fact, not the symptom: a close counts for a job only if it happened after that job's tab receipt was created (e.g. close events carry a sequence/time and are compared with the launch receipt, or claiming a tab in a new receipt retires that ID from `closedTabs` in every watcher generation including the handoff). Cover pi fresh launch, CLI fresh launch, resume into a reused ID, and a real close after launch still failing the job. Process-safety rules from pi-worker/03 stay as they are (exact PID+start, verified shell identity).

acceptance.text: A close event for a tab ID recorded before a job's launch receipt never marks that job failed, for pi and CLI fresh launches and for resume
A close of the job's own tab after launch still fails it and wakes main
The watcher handoff (reload) cannot resurrect a stale close for a reused ID
Tests reproduce the reused-ID case first (red before the fix)
Land gate passes

tickets.title: Hotfix: Claude CLI workers start again (the witness shim execs the PATH name, not the versioned realpath)
tickets.what: Observed 2026-11-25 20:37 and 20:39 after pi-worker/07 landed (b8abfebb): every frontend-imp job on claude fails with herdr's `timeout: timed out waiting for agent startup` (jobs j3a0711153840bab8, jeed4b400b88964c7); agy works (j62c48d2fc462b3ca, witness adopted). The shim did run and wrote witness.json, so claude started. Cause: `src/mcp/dispatch/harness-cli.ts:137` takes `real = executable(place.agent)` from `src/roles/roster.ts:114`, which returns `fs.realpathSync`. On this machine `~/.local/bin/claude` is a symlink to `~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.332`; the shim and `execWitness` (`src/runtime/cli-invocation.ts`) exec that versioned file, so the kernel names the process `2.1.332`, argv[0] is the versioned path, and herdr's `agent start --kind claude` never recognizes a claude agent. Fix: the launch execs the path as found on PATH (the symlink, e.g. `~/.local/bin/claude`) with argv[0] the agent name, in both the witness branch and the plain branch of the shim; keep `executable()`'s realpath for any caller that needs it (check each caller; don't change trust or identity checks that rely on the resolved file). Witness identity stays exact PID + start ticks. Add a test whose fake agent is a symlink to a versioned file name and assert the started process's `comm` and argv[0] are the agent name (red before the fix). Then main live-checks a claude job.

acceptance.text: A CLI agent reached through a symlink to a versioned file runs with comm and argv[0] equal to the agent name, through the witness branch and the plain branch
The witness still records the exact PID and start ticks of the agent process
Test with a symlinked versioned fake agent is red before the fix and green after
Land gate passes

tickets.title: Hotfix: finished job tabs close again when the owner's shell runs startup helpers
tickets.what: Observed 2026-11-25: since pi-worker/03 landed (a34ee9fb, watcher reload 20:06:59Z) no finished job tab closes; every reap in `~/.hud/watch.log` ends `exit=1` and `hud-reap` says `original shell identity or idle foreground unverified; not closing` (`src/runtime/reap-tab.ts:172-174`). Cause: `confirmIdleShells` (`src/runtime/tab-shell.ts:46-50`) refuses when any active process other than the shell is in the shell's session. The owner's zsh (powerlevel10k) starts helpers in that session at shell startup: `gitstatusd` and two zsh async workers reparented to the session's subreaper. Real case, job j6daafb3598870be7, shell 2675221 start 3338768: helpers started at 3338778 and 3338846, the agent (pi 2676358) at 3338948; a later prompt helper is a zombie. Fix the rule, not by name: session members that started before the worker's recorded start (pi STATUS `pid_start_time`, CLI witness `start`) are shell startup, not worker leftovers, and do not block the close; anything started after the worker started that is still active still refuses (a background job the worker left). Decide and test what happens to prompt helpers the shell spawns after the worker exits (p10k redraws the prompt): they must not block forever, and must not open a hole for a worker's own background child (which starts while the worker runs). Never match by process name. Tests use a real zsh with an rc that starts a daemon at startup and a helper per prompt (precmd), like p10k (pi-worker/07 lesson: no bare-shell fixtures). Also make the watcher log carry the reaper's refusal reason (today stderr is lost and the log only says exit=1). Process-killing code: extra review before land.

acceptance.text: A finished pi job and a finished CLI job in a real zsh tab whose rc starts a background daemon and per-prompt helpers are reaped and their tab closes
A background process started by the worker while it ran still blocks the close
No process is matched by name; identity stays exact PID + start ticks
watch.log shows the reaper's refusal reason on exit 1
Land gate passes after a separate review
